items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: You take a man like Sing, and Charlie, and that way... and that way. So, this note is right, that note is right... You tune with.

ctx.x: I think it's on the, there's one or two records, where you're definitely sharp, and I think it's records where, where there's a piano which, which is probably very flat, and probably causing it. Yes.

Because I, I don't know, you see me at night on the piano, and I always tune, because I hear a different thing. I know when I'm sharp. And I can tell how I hit, the north of the Gunner Street. And then the piano is, is not tuned with, so, Bill Russell uses it, you tune with. You take a man like Sing, and Charlie, and that way, and that way, and that way, and that way. So, this note is right, that note is right, just to, these sharp, you know. Yeah. You take, I'll tell you for instance, you take Thomas. Thomas…
Can you remember any of the early pieces you played, or first learned to play?
